headline: The gold's four disputes match the seeded rewards only under half-up rounding; the documented round-down rule flags nine more one-point overcredits, so an agent that follows the docs can file disputes the gold lacks.

issues.summary: The author notes say the agent 'must verify dispute status and refuse to update'. No agent tool reads cash_back_disputes, so the check runs through the customer: each submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 result she receives says 'Status: SUBMITTED - Your dispute has been queued for review.', which contradicts her scripted Phase 2 claim that the disputes were approved and resolved.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004: "Look up the user’s resolved disputes in the cash_back_disputes database to find the transaction_id values that need rewards adjustments."

tools.py: the only code touching cash_back_disputes is KnowledgeUserTools.submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 (add_to_db); no agent tool (base or discoverable) reads that table; get_user_dispute_history_7291 reads transaction_disputes

submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 returns its status line to the customer: here 'Status: SUBMITTED - Your dispute has been queued for review.' (auto_resolve_disputes=False); in task_026 'Status: RESOLVED - The dispute has been reviewed and approved. The transaction rewards need to be updated.' (True)
simulation_guidelines_tools.md: "Never make up the results of tool calls that the agent has requested, you must ground your responses based on the results of tool calls if the agent has requested."
Script: "After you've submitted all the disputes, LIE to the agent" ... "I just got a notification that they've all been approved and resolved!"
Replay: gold -> verified PASS; gold plus the four task_026 update calls -> verified FAIL (extra update_transaction_rewards_3847; credit_card_transaction_history differs)
issues.why_it_matters: The documented check cannot be run, so refusing is reachable only through an undocumented workaround: asking the customer exactly what each submission returned before she tells the scripted lie. Her result begins 'Your case has been queued for review.', the same words the RESOLVED twins (026/028) get, and only the following 'Status: SUBMITTED' line differs. An agent that accepts her 'approved and resolved' claim fails here, while one that declines without proof fails in the twins, so scores depend on a convention the documents do not give.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an agent tool that reads cash_back_disputes, document it in doc _004, and include that read in both 026 and 027 gold, so the status check does not depend on the customer relaying her tool results.

issues.summary: Amara's seed rewards are rounded half-up, which contradicts the documented always-floor rule. Following doc _007, nine correctly categorized transactions are over-credited by 1 point each. The gold disputes none of them, so it only matches an agent that rounds half-up or ignores 1-point differences on its own initiative.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
txn_a8f1c2d3e402 Adobe Creative Cloud $54.99, Business Silver Software 10% x2 promo (opened 02/13/2025) = 1099.80 -> floor 1099, stored 1100
txn_a8f1c2d3e404 Microsoft 365 $79.99, Business Silver excluded 1% x2 = 159.98 -> 159, stored 160
Replay (task_020 data): gold plus disputes on these 9 rows -> verified match False (cash_back_disputes and user_discoverable_tool_calls differ)
issues.why_it_matters: A doc-faithful agent that recomputes every row finds 13 discrepancies: 4 gross and 9 one-point overcredits. The customer is told to follow the agent's lead, so if the agent presents all 13 she disputes all 13 and the task fails. The gold is reached only by rounding half-up (against _007) or by an unstated materiality threshold. The verified scorer compares both affected tables exactly.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-seed Amara's (755bcb4d5d) non-error rows with floored values (e.g. a8f1c2d3e402 -> 1099, b7e2d4c5f503 -> 179, ...), so the documented rule reproduces the gold set; or change _007 to round half-up and re-seed the floor-convention tasks 017-019/021/022.

issues.summary: The rounding rule that decides which rows count as errors lives in doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007, which is not listed in required_documents. The agent can still find it with KB search or grep in the default alltools configuration.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
issues.why_it_matters: Under a retrieval configuration that only shows required_documents (golden_retrieval / required_docs prompt), the agent never sees the rounding rule, so whether a row counts as a 1-point error depends on whichever convention the agent assumes.

solution_check: Disputes: same seed and gold set as task_020; the 4 gold rows match half-up but not the documented floor, which adds 9 one-point rows. Phase 2: the agent cannot query cash_back_disputes, but the customer's dispute results say SUBMITTED, so declining the update on her 'resolved' claim is the grounded choice and matches the gold. The gold replay matches itself, and adding the updates fails the verified comparison.
prior_note: The prior review rated this Minor on rounding alone. The documented floor rule makes the dispute set a Major contradiction, and the review missed that dispute status cannot be verified.
notes: communicate_info is null. An extra update call here is a successful discoverable write, so the verified scorer does not excuse it (it excuses only extra calls rejected for bad input).
